lead: Two procedure stations: measuring blood pressure correctly in pregnancy, and testing urine with a dipstick (with explaining a midstream or 24-hour collection).
f: Rest 5 min, sitting or semi-recumbent 45°, feet flat, arm at heart level · cuff bladder covers ≥ 80% of the arm (large cuff if arm > 33 cm) · palpate systolic, inflate 30 mmHg above · deflate 2 mmHg/s · record to the nearest 2 mmHg
Systolic = K1 · diastolic = K5 (disappearance) · use K4 only if sounds go on to 0

sc: Silent gap from 150 to 130 → Auscultatory gap: palpate systolic first

f: Small cuff on a large arm: falsely high · large cuff: low · arm hanging below the heart: high · lying flat: supine hypotension

sc: Obese arm, standard cuff, 150/100 → Repeat with a large cuff

f: Hypertension ≥ 140/90 twice, 4 h apart · severe ≥ 160/110: treat now, re-check in 15 min · one high reading is not pre-eclampsia

sc: 145/95 twice, 4 h apart, at 30 wk → Hypertension: test urine for protein

f: Midstream (clean-catch) sample · check expiry · dip all pads about 1 s · read each pad at its own time against the chart
Protein 1+ ≈ 0.3 g/L → PCR · glucose 2+ → OGTT · ketones → hyperemesis, starvation · nitrites + leucocytes → MSU for culture (bacteriuria in 2–10%, always treat) · blood → infection, stones

sc: Nitrites and leucocytes positive → UTI: send MSU for culture

f: Significant proteinuria: PCR ≥ 30 mg/mmol or ≥ 0.3 g/24 h · 24-hour urine: discard the first sample, collect all for 24 h including the next morning's first

tr: Never round the BP to 0 or 5
